text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Pensioners will be allowed to take a job accoridng to new draft law designed to improve their living standard and avoid mass tax evasion.

- Baby food Milumil recently withdrawn from the British market on suspicion of bacterial infection comes to Croatia from a different (German) producer and is safe for use, says state office for food control.
- Croatia demands the young Serb suspected of killing the U.N. Belgian soldier and now in U.N. custody in East Slavonia, be tried by it own court.
- Agriculture minister Zlatko Domnikovic meets potato producers to negotiate protective prices and avoid unneeded import. Adequate storage turns out to be the biggest problem.
- Artists to enjoy 25 percent income tax cuts according to new regulations. Fines await some 100,000 tax payers who failed to register their income last year.
- Touroperator Bemextours says forecast for this year's tourist season seems optimistic. Early bookings indicate their plan to bring some 18,500 tourists to Croatia this yearmay be overshot.

- Croatian oil company INA and Italian AGIP which formed INAgip merger will invest $320 million and secure 230 million cubic meters of natural gas obtained from sites in northern Adriatic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
